title: Agent37 Review (2026): Pricing, Security & Features
summary: Agent37 provides a managed infrastructure layer that handles the persistent environment requirements for complex, autonomous coding swarms.
body_markdown:
## How to connect Agent37 to Activepieces workflows today


Activepieces treats every agent as a managed user, applying enterprise RBAC, SSO, and SCIM to govern what the swarm may connect to rather than just what a person may open.


Because Agent37 lacks a native integration in the Activepieces library, you, as the DevOps engineer responsible for the pipeline, must manually define the interface to ensure that agentic outputs reach downstream tools like Slack or Linear.


The following sequence establishes the connection through the standard REST interface:


1. Deploy agent instance in Agent37 dashboard
2. Copy the Cloud API endpoint and Auth Token
3. Add an HTTP Request integration in Activepieces
4. Map the JSON payload to the specific agent skill requirements


This configuration creates a verifiable audit trail for every request, allowing you to identify exactly where a handshake fails in a multi-step swarm.


### Option 1: The HTTP Request method for API triggers


The HTTP Request integration is the primary bridge for sending data from Activepieces to an Agent37 instance. By selecting the POST method and entering the specific endpoint URL, you can transmit structured data to specialized skills.


One example is the[YC Advisor](https://agent37.com/yc) which utilizes a knowledge base of 434 essays, interviews, and lectures to provide startup guidance. This method requires the manual entry of Bearer tokens in the request headers.


Every connector established in Activepieces is instantly available as an agent tool, meaning a single configuration serves both deterministic flows and autonomous swarms.


By registering a connection once, the platform exposes it via a per-project MCP server, allowing Agent37 to call any of the 1,000+ integrations without a second migration or manual schema export.


This dual-purpose architecture ensures that the same integration action running in a standard flow is the one reachable by your agents, a mechanism verifiable in the open-source Integrations Framework documentation.


### Option 2: Using the AI Step with custom providers


Activepieces includes a dedicated AI Step that can be reconfigured to point toward Agent37’s OpenAI-compatible API layer. By overriding the default Base URL, you can utilize models like Claude Sonnet 5.5 through the Agent37 proxy while maintaining the standard chat-completion format.


This approach simplifies the mapping process because the platform treats the autonomous agent as a standard LLM provider, reducing the complexity of the data transformation logic.


It's particularly effective for high-volume routing tasks where Claude Haiku 5.5 is employed to categorize incoming support tickets before the agent initiates a self-directed resolution path.


### Connecting Agent37 via MCP servers


For environments requiring deep integration with local files or private databases, bridging through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers allows Activepieces to interact with Agent37’s underlying toolset.


This setup involves hosting an intermediary server that translates Activepieces webhooks into MCP commands, which the agent then executes to perform complex reasoning tasks.


When using a high-reasoning model like Gemini 3.8 Flash for agentic coding, the model has the necessary context from your production environment. This bridge ensures the model has the necessary context from your production environment without exposing the entire database to the public internet.


The burden of maintenance is placed on your infrastructure team by this architecture. They must manage the uptime of the bridge server alongside the automation platform itself.
